podcast.body: "Just Like Honey," released by The Jesus and Mary Chain in 1985, was a single that was instrumental in establishing Creation Records as a significant force in British indie culture. "The Jesus and Mary Chain with just like honey, the single that established Creation records as a force in British indie culture in 1985."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: A song by The Jesus and Mary Chain, released in 1985, presented as an example of the experimental music emerging from the post-punk era. "Here's the Jesus and Marychain from 1985 with Just Like Honey."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Post-Punk Explosion Part 7: All the rest

podcast.body: Featured on their debut album, *Psycho Candy*, released in the fall of 1985, this song captivated listeners with its "big slab of fuzz" counterbalanced by a "lovely, breathy melody." The track, like the band's overall sound, laid essential groundwork for the shoegaze genre. "A big slab of fuzz that nevertheless had a lovely, breathy melody."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
